sentences.text: Respo  Prayer: Writ Petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution o  issuance of a Writ of Certiorarified Mandamus, calling for the reco  impugned order of the 1st respondent in G.O.Ms.No.58 dated 24.01.20  confirming the proceeding of Erode District Colle  Na.Ka.No.71946/1995/N6 dated 21.02.2018 and quash the same and  consequentially direct the respondents to consider allotment of any  available poramboke land or other lands in place of the existing ac  lands in S.No.1520/1.
For Petitioners : Mr.Naveen Kumar Murthi
For Respondents : Mr.A.Selvendran

Special Government Pleade  Page 2 of 7 https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis  
 ORDER [Order of the Court was made by S.M.SUBRAMANIAM, J.]
The order of the Government issued in G.O.Ms.No.58, Revenue and Disaster Management Department dated 24.01.2020 is sought to be quashed in the present writ proceeding.

2. It is not in dispute that the subject property described in the present writ petition has been acquired for public purposes by the Government by invoking the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act.
The compensation due to the erstwhile owner had already been settled.

The Government in its order had stated that the petitioners have already filed 10 litigations questioning the acquisition of land for public purposes and all the cases were rejected against the writ petitioners.

sentences.text: The petitioners submitted a representation to re-convey the land.
The Government has rejected the claim of the petitioners to re-convey the land.
Re-conveyance of the acquired lands cannot be claimed as an absolute right.
Re-conveyance is the discretion of the Government to be granted, if the lands https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis acquired are not utilised.
4. However, it is not necessary that the lands acquired are to be utilised only for the purpose for it was acquired.

Even the Government is empowered to utilise the land for any other public purposes,
since the Government after acquisition became the absolute owner of the property.

In other words,
the acquired lands vest with the Government and thus, the re-conveyance cannot be claimed as a matter of right.

5. In the present case, the Government considered the claim of the petitioners and rejected the representation seeking re-conveyance of the acquired lands and High Court in exercise of powers of judicial review has no reason to interfere with such a decision taken by the Government in public interest.
6.
The respondents are directed to take possession of the acquired property immediately, if not taken already and utilise the land for public purposes in the manner known to law.
The possession is directed to be taken within a period of four (4) weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis order.
7. Accordingly, this Writ Petition stands dismissed.
No costs.
Consequently, connected Miscellaneous Petitions are closed.
